items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the civil service law, in relation to background checks for
police transfer candidates
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7376

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to background checks
for police transfer candidates

 
PURPOSE:

This bill amends Civil Service Law (CSL) 50 subdivision 4, to remove a
conflict with the emergency regulations promulgated by the New York
State Division of Criminal Justice Services (DCJS). The bill would
remove the background check prohibitions in CSL 50.4 as it relates to
police officers and allow for police candidates to be given the requi-
site background checks pursuant to 9 New York Codes, Rules and Regu-
lations Part 6000. The amendment is a simple technical fix that will
align the CSL with the DCJS emergency regulations.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill adds language to the third unnumbered paragraph in
CSL 50.4. It amends the background check prohibitions of the section to
exclude police officer positions.

Section 2 of the bill provides that the bill shall take effect

immediately.

 
EXISTING LAW:

CSL section 50.4 provides that background checks and fingerprinting may
be conducted on applicants. However, the section prohibits background
checks of candidates who are current employees, who transfer pursuant to
CSL section 70, who are on a preferred list pursuant to CSL section 81,
or whose names are on an eligible list as defined by CSL section 56 and
have completed a promotion exam subject to CSL section 52. Presently,
these prohibitions would exclude police candidates who transfer or
promote pursuant to the above sections to be fingerprinted and back-
ground checked.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new proposal.

 
STATEMENT IN SUPPORT:

The New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services put forth emer-
gency regulations that relate to the background investigations of
persons seeking permanent appointment in the competitive class of the
civil service as police officers. The regulations seek to ensure that
all persons appointed to the position of police officer are held to the
same hiring standards and promote professional police services.  The
regulations require that all candidates, including employees who trans-
fer, undergo background checks. The Department of Civil Service is
supportive of the intent to ensure that all competitive police employees
are held to the same background check standards. To that end, the
Department proposes amending CSL section 50.4, to allow background
checks of police employees who transfer through CSL section 70. The
proposed amendment is a simple technical fix that excepts prospective
police employees from the CSL section 50.4 prohibitions on background
checks and resolves the conflict with the DCJS emergency regulations.

 
BUDGET IMPLICATIONS:

None

summary: Provides for background checks for police transfer candidates.
